basic_identification.sector_category: Chemical / Occupational Safety and Health (approved by the Chemical Division Council and finalized by the Occupational Safety and Health and Chemical Hazards Sectional Committee, CHD 8, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Occupational Safety and Health and Chemical Hazards Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements for an Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) management system to enable an organization to control its OH&S risks, formulate a safety policy, and continually improve its overall performance.

version_status_and_amendments.year_first_published: 2000 (adopted on 22 February 2000, taking considerable guidance from BS 8800 : 1996)
version_status_and_amendments.superseded_by: Modern systems have transitioned to IS/ISO 45001 : 2018 (Occupational health and safety management systems — Requirements with guidance for use)
version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No active amendments have been issued on this reaffirmed copy (NIL on this copy).

allied_standards.title: Drinking Water — Specification (Second Revision)
allied_standards.relevance: Ensures potability of water, which is audited under occupational welfare, sanitation, and eye-wash station requirements.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Management Systems Standard / Occupational Guidelines (Chemical Department / Occupational Safety and Health)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary System Certification. Since IS 18001 is a management system standard rather than a physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual physical 'ISI Mark' standard mark on a consumer label. Instead, organizations apply to accredited third-party registrars (such as the BIS Management Systems Certification Department) to undergo a rigorous multi-stage audit and obtain an official 'OHSMS Certificate of Registration' [1]. This certification enhances public image, minimizes liability risks, and demonstrates strict compliance with India's central and state Factories Acts [2, 3].

requirements.detail: Top management must define, document, and endorse an OH&S policy that is appropriate to the nature and scale of the organization's risks, includes a commitment to continual improvement and legal compliance, is made known to all employees, and is reviewed periodically [4, 5].

Requires identifying, accessing, and tracking central, state, and local legal requirements (and changes thereto) attributable to the organization's activities and hazards, ensuring relevant information is communicated to employees [6, 7].

Top management must designate, document, and communicate OH&S responsibilities, authorities, and reporting lines for all levels—including sub-contractors and visitors. A senior management representative must be assigned to oversee the OHSMS [4, 8].

Requires identifying operations associated with significant risks and executing them under specified conditions. This mandates implementing procedures for personal protective equipment (PPE) control, access segregation, and high-integrity testing of operator protection, physical guarding, and automatic shutdown systems [9-11].

Mandates establishing and periodically testing procedures to identify and respond to emergency situations. For large installations, plans must be prepared in consultation with municipal or state disaster planning teams. Appropriate first-aid facilities must be matched to site hazards, including stabilization protocols for remote sites [12, 13].

A mandatory post-incident recovery plan (CIRP) must be established, covering: clear responsibilities, confidential post-trauma 'defusing' immediately after the event, emotional 'de-briefing' for employees, and counseling for victims' families [14, 15].

Requires establishing and maintaining procedures for the identification, storage, protection, retrieval, retention, and disposal of records to demonstrate system conformity and trace performance outcomes [16].

Requires conducting internal audits of the OH&S management system at planned intervals to verify that the system conforms to planned arrangements, has been properly implemented and maintained, and to identify areas for continual improvement [16].

Establishes a three-dimensional matrix to evaluate risk levels (Trivial, Tolerable, Moderate, Substantial, or Intolerable) based on the probability of occurrence (Highly Unlikely, Unlikely, Likely) and the severity of harm (Slightly Harmful, Harmful, Extremely Harmful) [17].

Requires reviewing any proposed risk control action plan before implementation, checking if revised controls achieve tolerable levels, if new hazards are created, and if the solution is cost-effective and accepted by employees [18].

To determine compliance with the specifications of this standard, the final observed or calculated value of any physical measurement, noise level, or air monitoring result must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value [19].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 18001 : 2007 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification establishing requirements and guidance for implementing an Occupational Health and Safety Management System (OHSMS). Maintained under the Occupational Safety and Health and Chemical Hazards Sectional Committee (CHD 8) and reaffirmed in 2023, this standard unifies safety management practices into a cohesive Plan-Do-Check-Act framework. It mandates developing a comprehensive safety policy, identifying and tracking legal obligations, allocating senior management representatives, and enforcing operational controls (such as PPE maintenance and emergency shutdown systems). It also unifies advanced field protocols—including detailed hazard identification questions, a multi-tier risk estimator matrix, and a critical incident recovery plan (providing post-trauma defusing and de-briefing)—ensuring maximum worker safety, risk mitigation, and regulatory compliance across Indian industries.
